items.text:
Peak Master 450 LP on Kog'Maw (fresh account). Now low Diamond 4.
Goal: Challenger. Complaints: no mobility, dies to assassins,
hard to play for objectives. First principles only: no win rates.

Keep Kog'Maw. Add one pocket pick.
Stay ADC.

• Your edge at Master was mastery: hundreds of
games of Kog ranges, spacing and spikes. A new
main throws that away and rebuilds it from
Diamond.
• All three complaints follow you to any ADC
that does real damage. Mobile ADCs die later.
They still die.
• Kog's real weakness is the draft: he needs a
team in front of him. That is a some-games
problem, so fix it with a second champion for
those games, not a new main.
• You decayed. Rust feels like "my champion is
bad". Judge after 30 to 50 games back, not 10.

You climbed one tier per season. That is real,
steady improvement, and you should be proud of it.

But Master 450 to Challenger is not one more tier
of the same. It is the gap between knowing Kog
and never dying for nothing.

Most of your deaths to assassins were decided
10 seconds earlier, by where you stood.
That is the skill to learn. No champion skips it.

Same auto-attack spacing you already know.
Her R makes you untargetable through the dive,
her E roots the diver. Lock her when they show
2+ divers and your team has no peel.

• You are bored of Kog, not just frustrated.
Fun is your goal #1, and a bored one-trick
stops queuing.
• In 50 games your death notes (tab 5) say "I
stood right and still died for nothing". Then
switch ADC, not role.

• Kog has no answer of his own to a dive. His
safety is made by teammates, and solo queue
does not let you pick them.
• Every Master+ player knows to dive Kog. You
are the target every single game.
• Self-reliant champions (a dash, an
untargetable spell) let you fix your own
mistakes. Kog punishes each one with a death.
• A weak early game means lanes against
bullies give the first 10 minutes away, and
some games are decided by then.

• W hits for a % of max health from long
range. Few carries melt tanks and objectives
from that far.
• Mastery is the biggest edge at high rank.
You have it on Kog and on nothing else.
• Being the target is a weapon: if they always
dive you, you know the fight before it starts,
and can pull it into your team.
• You reached Master 450 on a fresh account
with him. People play Kog in NA Challenger (we
pulled their builds on the Doran's page).
• Switching resets what you know about the
champion. It does not reset why you die.

Both sides are right about something. The switch case is really about drafts:
some games, Kog has no one in front of him. That is solved by a pocket pick
for those games. The stay case is about everything else, and everything else
is most games. Do not trade your best tool for a fix to a minority of games.

True: Flash is your only escape. One
misstep and there is no button to undo
it.

Mobility fixes mistakes after they happen. A
Challenger Kog avoids them before: standing
spot, wave, timing. Ask "if they jump me now,
who stands between us?" If nobody, you are
already wrong.

Mostly you.
Kog just makes
it visible.

True: assassins exist to kill immobile
carries, and Kog is their favourite.

Most deaths start with not knowing where the
assassin is. A death that pulls their whole
kit onto you while your team kills them is a
fair trade. Dying alone in a side lane is not.

Mostly you.
Ranges and windows:
"carry into fed
assassins" page.

True: Kog cannot walk in first or
flank, so he cannot start a contest.

Kog is one of the best objective takers there
is: W shreds big health pools. The problem is
arriving late or into fog. Objective fights
are won 60 s before the spawn. See tab 4.

An assassin you cannot see is in the fog closest to you.
Never be the closest one to that fog.
You are the first thing he reaches.
He has to go through your team.
Objective fights are won before the objective spawns
For dragon, grubs, herald and baron. Kog cannot start a contest, so he arrives first.

Check your wave.
Where will it be
at −60?

Shove the wave on the
objective's side of the map.

Back and buy.
Never walk in
with 1,000 gold.

Walk in with your support.
Sweep the entrance together.

Hold the side of the pit
away from their fog.
R checks bushes for free.

• Do not face-check the pit. That is the "hard
to play objectives" feeling: walking second
into fog.
• Trade instead: plates, a tower or the other
objective on the far side.
• Or give it and live. A dead Kog at 25
minutes costs more than one dragon.

• Once you are set up, W takes the objective
faster than almost anyone, from behind your
team.
• Their only answer is to walk through your
team to reach you. That is the fight you want.
• Dragon spawns on your side of the map. Bot
lane wave control is the whole setup.
Seven habits. My bet: the first three move you most.

Every fight: name where each assassin is. Unseen means
the closest fog to you. Never be closest.

Before each step forward. If the answer is nobody, step
back.

Step up right after their engage is spent, never before.
Their ult down is your fight.

Shove and back 60 s before every objective. Arrive first
or trade elsewhere.

Enemy shows 2+ divers and your team has no peel: Xayah.
Otherwise Kog.

After each game, look at your first death only. One
line: where was I, did I know where the killer was?

Challenger is many good games, not the most games.
Tilted games undo good ones.

Write the one-line death note every game.
After 50 games, count two piles:
"did not know where they were" vs "stood right, died anyway".
If the first pile is bigger (I expect it will be),
the fix is habits, and Kog stays.
If the second pile is bigger, come back and we revisit.

source.method: Coaching opinion from first principles. No win rates or stats were used.
source.note: Icons: Data Dragon 16.22.1. Rank history as told by Noah in the project chat.
